To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed approach can be used in a real space mission, since it has been extensively validated in a ground simulation environment.
the proposed visual localization approach is robust and reliable for on orbit servicing applications.

the proposed visual localization system based only on intensity edges and robust against illumination and background clutter, can achieve an average accuracy of 1.5 m at mid range and 0.3 m at close range, with an update rate of 10 Hz, using a monocular and a stereo camera respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: (i) the design of a visual system based on a monocular camera at mid range and on a stereo camera at close proximity, to deal with the challenging conditions in space, (ii) the development of detection and tracking methods to deal with the above issues, (iii) a ground verification campaign to assess the performance of the proposed system.

the development of a vision based localization system to support on orbit servicing missions, which is able to deal with the challenging conditions of space, such as the direct sunlight illumination, the satellite surface reflectivity, the partial cooperation of the target satellite, and the high dynamics of the approach.

the design and development of a visual based localization system, to be integrated on board of a servicer, that is able to provide a robust, accurate and low cost solution for on orbit servicing missions, with the main goal of reducing the risk of collision, by providing the servicer with the capability of tracking the target at a safe distance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our system is able to track the satellite with an accuracy of 0.1 m at a distance of 5 m, with a latency of 1.3 s, while at a distance of about 20 m it is able to detect the satellite and to estimate the range with a latency of about 1 s.

the proposed approach can be considered an effective and reliable solution for visual localization in space, with an acceptable accuracy, robustness and reliability, as required by the challenging space applications.
, although a visual localization system is a promising solution, the current state of the art is not yet ready to be employed for a fully operational on orbit rendezvous mission.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed approach provides a robust and accurate localization system for the mid and close range phases of a rendezvous and docking operation between a servicer spacecraft and a target, which is passive and does not have any active or passive markers, but is supposed to keep a controlled orientation, with small fluctuations.

, by means of the proposed approach, a servicer is able to perform a rendezvous with a partially cooperative satellite, with a very low risk and a very high level of precision, even in the most challenging conditions of space.

, in the future, a vision based localization system will be an important tool for the autonomous docking of a servicer with a partially cooperative satellite, especially when the servicer has no prior knowledge about the target, such as the case of the servicing of a failed satellite.
The main takeaway from our work is that

visual localization is possible even in very challenging scenarios, and that the use of ground in the loop information, i.e. transmitted images to ground and the corresponding pose estimates from a ground station, is a very promising approach to aid rendezvous maneuvers.

the proposed system can be easily implemented on board of a servicer satellite and it can be employed to provide the necessary information for the execution of a docking maneuver with a partially cooperative, non marked target.

, even in the presence of challenging lighting conditions and surface properties, the proposed approach can be successfully employed to perform the final stages of rendezvous and docking operations between a servicer spacecraft and an on orbit target satellite, in particular for the purpose of on orbit servicing.
